title: OpenAI Ecosystem and Interfaces
summary: This intermediate module teaches learners to identify a documented OpenAI interface, evaluate whether it fits a software task, and verify interface details against the official documentation. After completing it, learners can make a source-supported interface choice instead of relying on an unverified description.
objectives: Identify the documented boundary between an application and an OpenAI capability.
Evaluate an interface by checking its documented inputs, outputs, constraints, and failure behavior.
Verify interface information against the cited official source before using it in a design.
Explain which source changed in this update and what material the correction affected.

sections.title: Level and scope
paragraphs: This is an intermediate module. It assumes that you can read technical documentation and understand that software exchanges inputs and outputs across an interface. It does not assume prior knowledge of a particular OpenAI interface, version, or configuration.

For this module, an interface is the documented boundary through which an application provides input and receives output. The ecosystem is the surrounding set of provider documentation and documented capabilities that a developer considers when choosing that boundary.

sections.title: Evaluating an interface
paragraphs: Begin with the task your application must perform. Describe the required input, expected output, acceptable failure behavior, and any operational constraints before selecting an interface. This prevents the interface name from becoming a substitute for a clear requirement.

Next, consult the official documentation and confirm that the documented interface accepts the input you have, can produce the output you need, and describes relevant constraints and failure behavior. If a required detail is absent from the documentation, treat that detail as UNKNOWN rather than assuming it.

Finally, test the documented behavior with a small representative case before integrating it into a larger system. Record the documentation page and verification date so that a later review can distinguish a changed source from an implementation defect.
sections.callout: Do not infer a specific interface, version, or configuration from this module. Confirm those details in the current official documentation.

sections.title: Source correction
paragraphs: The prior cited source was the local module file identified in the update request. Its publisher was unregistered and it had never been verified. This update replaces that source record with the official OpenAI developer documentation.

The change affects source attribution and the guidance for verifying available interfaces. Unsupported claims about specific interfaces, versions, and configuration details are omitted. The retained learning method is to define requirements, inspect the official documentation, compare documented behavior with those requirements, and test a representative case.

sections.title: What you can do now
paragraphs: After completing this module, you can turn an application requirement into a documentation review: identify the needed inputs and outputs, locate a documented OpenAI interface, check its constraints and failure behavior, and test it before integration. You can also recognize when a claim is UNKNOWN because the official source does not support it.

questions.prompt: What source change does this update make?
choices: It replaces an unregistered, never-verified local source record with the official OpenAI developer documentation.
It adds an unsupported version number to the prior local source.
It removes the need to verify interface details.
It treats undocumented configuration details as established facts.
questions.explanation: The source-correction section states that the prior local source record was unregistered and never verified, and that this update replaces it with the official OpenAI developer documentation.

questions.prompt: Which process does the module recommend before integrating an OpenAI interface?
choices: Choose an interface by name and infer any missing constraints.
Define requirements, inspect official documentation, compare documented behavior with the requirements, and test a representative case.
Rely on the prior local source without checking its publisher.
Assume that undocumented behavior will remain stable.
questions.explanation: The module directs learners to define the task, inspect the official documentation, compare documented behavior with requirements, and test a small representative case.

questions.prompt: How should a learner handle a required detail that is absent from the official documentation?
choices: Treat it as UNKNOWN rather than assume it.
Treat the missing detail as guaranteed behavior.
questions.explanation: The evaluating-an-interface section says that a required detail absent from the documentation must be treated as UNKNOWN rather than assumed.
